text:
carol: Heads-up — eval dashboard shows an embedding regression on s-bench after the runner config change merged yesterday (model=q4-small-v2). mean cosine dropped ~3.2% vs baseline. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

dmitri: Which pipeline/runner? link: https://dash.internal.redwood/s-bench/overview  (shows the drop around 21:10 UTC)

carol: It's the new eval-runner instances (runner v2.9.0) — the CI canary passed but full eval sweep shows the delta. I attached sample outputs to the job artifacts.

alice: Reproduced locally on my laptop with minimal harness config. Quick repro:
```bash
git checkout runners/main
python -m eval_runner --suite s-bench --model q4-small-v2 --seed 42 --save-embeddings out.json
python -c "import numpy as np, json; a=json.load(open('out.json')); print(np.mean(a['cosine']))"
```
Average cosine is ~0.842 vs baseline 0.871.

ben: Log snippet from my run — I see a fallback to a slow quant kernel for small sequence lengths: 
```
[2026-03-19T21:09:13Z] INFO  runner::kernel_selector - selected kernel: qkv_split_quant_fallback
[2026-03-19T21:09:13Z] WARN  runner::execution - using software FP16 path for attention (latency penalty)
```
Could the fallback change internal rounding/padding that affects embedding normalization?

alice: I also noticed tokenizer version bump in the harness config: `tokenizers==0.15.2 -> 0.16.0` in the same PR. Tokenization drift could change positions/prefixes that affect pooled embeddings.

dmitri: Good catch. Two parallel suspects: kernel fallback (runtime) vs tokenizer bump (preproc). We should narrow which side explains the cosine drop. Quick A/B: run with new runner + old tokenizer, and old runner + new tokenizer.

eva: Recommend holding the rollout (canary) and pinning eval-runner to previous image for production evals until triage done. I'll open a canary hold ticket and pin image in the console. :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: CI job 2103456875 finished — eval-s-bench artifacts: https://ci.internal.redwood/artifacts/2103456875. Failing metric: embedding_cosine_mean (delta -0.029). Logs attached: artifacts/runner.log, artifacts/tokenizer.log

ben: Ran the A/B: 
- new-runner + old-tokenizer -> cosine ~0.869 (near baseline)
- old-runner + new-tokenizer -> cosine ~0.844 (matches regression)
So tokenizer bump is the likely culprit. Repro steps and diffs in my gist: https://gist.internal/ben/tokenizer-diff

carol: Nice. If tokenizer change is the root, what's the plan? Revert tokenizer in harness to 0.15.2 for the evaluation pipeline and schedule a dedicated tokenizer QA pass (regression tests on embeddings) before we bump again.

dmitri: Will open a revert PR for the harness dep and add a unit test that checks embedding baseline on a small canonical prompt set. Also add a note to the model-onboarding checklist to run tokenization diff tests.

eva: I'll roll back the eval-runner image for canary and re-run the full s-bench job once revert PR merges. If the metrics return to baseline, we can then scope the tokenizer change separately.

carol: Action items: 1) dmitri -> revert dep PR + unit test; 2) eva -> pin canary + re-run full sweep; 3) ben/alice -> tokenization diff doc and short eval harness script to detect emb shifts. I'll mark this thread as blocker for the release until embedding_cosine_mean recovers. :thumbsup:

ben: FYI, tokenizer diff showed a subtle whitespace-handling tweak on the pre-token normalization step. I'll propose a minimal patch to preserve old normalization behavior while allowing the newer tokenizer for other fixes.

carol: Great. Thanks all — keep updates here.
